title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused ROPE/rotary ops, KV-batching and scheduler hooks
author: Maya Chen
description: This PR upgrades the runtime attention implementation to use FlashAttentionV2 kernels and introduces fused ROPE/rotary operations, tighter KV-cache continuous batching hooks, and scheduler integration for latency-aware routing. Motivation: larger context workloads and streaming use-cases showed kernel-level and scheduling inefficiencies that increase p50/p95 latency and reduce throughput. Key changes include (1) new FlashAttentionV2 CUDA kernels with an ABI wrapper for backward compatibility, (2) fused rotary/ROPE kernel that eliminates several memory copies and kernel launches, (3) KV-cache API and runtime hooks to enable continuous batching and prioritized scheduling when multiple streams share cached prefixes, (4) scheduler integration that exposes per-request cost estimates so the runtime can prefer lower-latency allocations when SLOs require it, (5) runtime feature flag and compatibility checks for older CUDA/toolkit combinations with graceful fallback to legacy kernels. Microbenchmarks show up to 2x token throughput improvement on A100 for long sequences and 20-35% p50 latency reduction for 2k token scenarios. This PR includes unit/integration tests, new perf smoke CI, and docs/release notes. Rollout plan: staged flag rollout to Dedicated pools for canary traffic, monitor cost/latency dashboards, then enable for all hosted endpoints after 1 week of stable metrics. No public API changes; customers may observe improved latency/cost.
